other_side: Zitron's answer to the solopreneur golden age is that the ground it stands on is subsidised. He argues subscribers are getting "$30 to $40 of compute for a dollar", and paraphrasing Doctorow, that selling forty dollars for one "is not a real business" nor organic demand. The cheap tools minting solo founders are, on his reading, loss-leaders from two firms with no path to profitability, and he mocks the output as subsidised plans producing "calorie tracking apps that get two users". He also reads this edition's other headline, Nvidia backstopping the Neoclouds, the opposite way to NLW's sources: if Nvidia has to guarantee demand for its own customers' GPUs, that is evidence real demand "does not exist at scale". When the subsidies stop, he says, so does the boom.
truth_beneath: The variable both men orbit is whether ground-level AI usage creates value that survives true-cost pricing. Both accept two facts: Stripe and Census data show a real surge in solo business formation and faster million-dollar cohorts, and end users currently buy compute far below what it costs to serve. The empirical question that will resolve is whether the 2025-26 solopreneur cohorts keep their revenue once tokens are repriced — the observable to watch is cohort survival and formation rates in Stripe's next data releases as spending caps like Tesla's spread and subscriptions move toward cost. The residue is pure worldview: a general-purpose technology diffusing to individuals, or manufactured consent propping up two unprofitable labs. NLW is vindicated if solo founders keep hitting a million at full-price tokens; Zitron if the boom deflates with the subsidies. Both are polemicists with incentives — NLW bullish and builder-facing, Zitron bubble-certain and anti-hype — so the signal is where they agree: the subsidy era is ending. Watch the next solopreneur cohort numbers against token repricing.
